sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Achal Kumar Paliwal
 On The 12th Of August, 2024
 Misc. Appeal No. 1243 of 2006
 National Insurance Company Ltd.
 Versus
 Smt.Kusum And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Rakesh Jain - Advocate for the appellant.
None for the respondent.

Order 
This appeal has been filed by the appellant/insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act arising out of award dated 24.12.2005 passed by 9th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal, in MCC No. 129/2005 seeking exoneration from liability to pay the compensation/ setting aside of impugned award/reduction of compensation amount.

entities.text: 9th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company submits that on the date of accident, rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence.
It is also evident from para 9 of the impugned award.
Tribunal has wrongly assumed that on the date of accident, rider of motorcycle would be having learning licence, whereas, there is no evidence with respect to same.
It is also urged that in the instant case, owner and rider of the motorcycle were present before before the tribunal.
They did not adduce any evidence with respect to licence.
On above grounds, it is 2 MA-1243-2006 urged that the appeal be allowed and insurance company be exonerated from liability to pay compensation amount.
3. I have heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record of the case.
4. It is evident from para 9 of the impugned award that on the date of accident, rider of the motorcycle was not having valid and effective driving licence/ he was not duly licenced.

5. So far as rider of the offending vehicle having learning licence on the date of accident is concerned, in the instant case, owner and rider of the offending vehicle were present before the tribunal and they also filed reply to application filed by the claimant but they did not adduce any National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Smt.Kusum on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180717564/
1 evidence before the tribunal to the effect that on the date of accident, rider of the motorcycle was having learning driving licence.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Smt.Kusum
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, in this Court's opinion, tribunal wrongly placed burden upon appellant/insurance company and wrongly presumed that on the date of accident, rider of the motorcycle would be having learning driving licence.

6. Therefore, appeal filed by the appellant is allowed and insurance company is exonerated from liability to pay the compensation and it is held that driver and owner of offending vehicle are liable to pay compensation jointly and severally.
Findings of tribunal with respect to liability to pay the compensation stands modified to the extent as indicated above.
7. In the instant case, deceased was clearly third party.
Therefore, in the instant case, it would be appropriate to apply principle of pay and 3 MA-1243-2006 recover.

8. Appellant Insurance Company shall at the first instance / shall first pay the adjudged compensation along with interest as adjudged to respondents/non-applicants, the insurance company shall be entitled/shall be at liberty to recover the same from respondent Nos.5 and 6,
respectively driver and owner of the offending vehicle, in the manner as provided in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Swaran Singh & Others, 2004 ACJ I (SC), Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd., AIR 2018 SC 2662, Shammana Vs. Divisional Manager of Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. AIR 2018 SC 3726/Sec.174 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
